01.r: Joseph fixed the arrangement as lasting law.
01.n: Gesenius gives the general sense 'to put, to set, to place'; BDB lists setting 'a law, statute' among its uses. The 'And' at the head of our sentence belongs to this verb.

02.r: The arrangement of the fifth just agreed.
02.n: The object marker with 'it' attached: 'it' is feminine, referring to the arrangement as a whole.

03.r: Pharaoh's governor, who made the arrangement.

04.r: A standing rule, not a one time measure.
04.n: Gesenius: properly 'that which is established or definite', and so an appointed portion or a statute. The brief's lexicon lists 'prescribed due' among its senses, which fits a fixed share of the harvest.

05.r: The rule still stood when the account was written.

08.r: The rule covers the ground of Egypt.

09.n: The word for ground, tilled land, as in Genesis 47:20 on this page; we render it 'ground' to keep it apart from the general word for 'land'. YLT does the same.

11.r: The share is the king's by right.
11.n: The Hebrew says only 'to Pharaoh'; the 'to' marks ownership, and our 'belongs' spells that out in English.

12.n: Gesenius: a fifth part, and specially the fifth part of produce, which the Egyptians paid as a tax, citing this verse, the only place the word occurs.

13.n: The brief's lexicon lists 'only' and 'save, except'. The KJV and Geneva say 'except', and put 'only' later for the word we render 'alone'.

15.r: Egypt's priests, whose land was not sold.
15.n: BDB lists this verse among the places where the word is used of Egyptian priests.

16.r: Theirs was the only ground left out.

17.r: Denies that it passed to Pharaoh.

18.r: The priests' ground never passed to the king.
18.n: The same expression as in Genesis 47:20 on this page, 'it was to Pharaoh', here denied.

01.n: τίθημι, to put, set: the same picture as the Hebrew.

02.n: αὐτοῖς, 'for them', where the Hebrew has 'it': the Greek has Joseph set the statute for the people.

12.n: ἀποπεμπτόω, to pay a fifth: the Greek turns the noun into a verb, 'to pay the fifth to Pharaoh'.
